chapter: Teddy Wilson bands and Cafe Society
title: Trio with Bill Coleman and Ellis Larkins at Cafe Society Uptown
summary: Hall and Coleman form a trumpet, bass and piano trio that became a success until they asked for a raise.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, when did Bill go back to Paris? 1949!
So, Billy Moore had the trio, the alternate for Teddy at the Cafe Uptown, it was during the

war, and the bass player's name was West, his last name was West, I can't think of his first name, and Billy Moore got sick and Ellis Larkins was a pianist so John Hammond called Bill Coleman and I to make a trio and we were opposite Teddy Wilson group. We got rehired. And we stayed there a year and something.
So here you were hired by the same man that didn't want you?
Why did he have a sudden change of heart?
Well, not sudden, but a change of heart?
We will lead up to that, to the present time, the same person, okay?
Okay, right. The career has definitely been intertwined over the years, hasn't it?
Yeah, yeah. But always in connection with this person, you know? And we were an instant success.
So it was just trumpet, bass and piano, huh?
They never heard of it before. And Bill plays so beautifully and so tastefully, it wasn't offensive
and we stayed there a long time. We stayed there long enough to ask for a raise and get fired. (Laughter)
According to these dates, if they are accurate, it says '42 and '43.
Well, so you think it was '42 and '43?
Yeah, I guess so, I guess it was '42 and '43. When you mention years, I have to think about the birth of my kids to associate what I was doing at that time.
